subject: اللغة الإنجليزية
lesson: Lesson 3: Grammar – Zero and first conditionals
outcomes: Know the difference between zero and first conditionals.
Talk about what you will do in different situations.

tf.s: The zero conditional talks about things that are always true.
tf.why: Yes, zero = real situations that are always true.

tf.s: The first conditional uses if + Present simple, will + verb.
tf.why: Correct! e.g. If it rains, I'll stay home.

tf.s: The zero conditional uses will in both parts.
tf.why: The zero conditional uses the Present simple in both parts.

tf.s: 'If you mix yellow and blue paint, you make green' is a first conditional.
tf.why: It is always true, so it is a zero conditional.

tf.s: The first conditional is about things that might happen in the future.
tf.why: Right, it talks about possible future events.

tf.s: 'If we all buy everything online, shops will close' is a first conditional.
tf.why: Well done: if + Present simple, will + verb.

tf.s: We say 'If it will rain tomorrow, I will stay home.'
tf.why: No will after if: If it rains tomorrow, I'll stay home.

tf.s: Huda's banana was grown in Oman.
tf.why: Yes, it was grown in Oman.

tf.s: Huda will ask her teacher to find out more.
tf.why: Huda and her mum will look online.

tf.s: 'If you don't eat breakfast, you get hungry' is a zero conditional.
tf.why: Good! It is a general truth.

boxes.q: Which conditional is about things that are always true?
boxes.why: The zero conditional is for general truths.

Complete: If you ___ (not eat) breakfast, you get hungry.
boxes.why: Zero conditional: Present simple in the if part.

boxes.q: Complete: If the cat falls from that tree, I ___ it.

boxes.why: The banana was grown in Oman.

boxes.why: Her project is over the holidays.

boxes.q: How will Huda find out more?
Which verb goes in the if part of a first conditional?
boxes.why: The if part uses the Present simple.

boxes.q: Buying food grown in your own country is called buying ...
boxes.why: Buy locally = buy things made or grown near you.

mcq.q: What is the form of the first conditional?
mcq.why: First conditional: if + Present simple, will + verb.

mcq.q: What is the form of the zero conditional?
mcq.why: Zero conditional uses the Present simple in both parts.

mcq.q: When do we use the zero conditional?
o: for things that are always true
buy things made or grown near where you live
mcq.why: Buying locally means buying things from your own area or country.

o: If it rains tomorrow, I'll stay at home.
If it will rain tomorrow, I stay at home.
If it rained tomorrow, I will stay at home.
If it rain tomorrow, I'll staying home.
mcq.why: No will after if: If it rains, I'll...

mcq.q: Complete: If I have time this Saturday, I ___ a new book.
Complete: If you heat ice, it ___.
mcq.why: It is always true, so we use the zero conditional: melts.

mcq.q: Zero or first? 'If you mix yellow and blue paint, you make green.'
o: zero, because it is always true
first, because it is in the future
mcq.why: It is a general truth, so it is zero.

mcq.q: Why is 'If we all buy everything online, shops will close' a first conditional?
o: It is about a possible result in the future.
mcq.why: It shows a possible future result.

mcq.q: Which sentence is a general truth, not a future plan?
o: If you don't eat breakfast, you get hungry.
If I go to the mall, I'll buy shoes.
If it rains, we'll stay inside.
If I lose my wallet, I'll tell Dad.
mcq.why: It is always true, so it is a zero conditional.
